source.title: Knowing, and Saying It Only When Asked: LLM Endognostics and the Schizognosis of Minerva-7B

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures internal risk-sensitive contrastive scores alongside paired behavioral outcomes, providing a conceptual test of whether risk-related internal information can differ when overt behavior does not. It does not test the original refusal-direction intervention.
record.gate_note: The study cites the original refusal-direction paper but does not find, remove, or add its harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. It reports a Jacobian-lens contrastive margin for risky versus safe prompts and behavioral outcomes for those pairs, so those results bear on V5. The factual falsehood experiments and linear-probe comparisons concern factual knowledge and verbalization, not refusal or the refusal direction, and are not cataloged as rows. No causal intervention on the contrastive risk margin was performed.
record.test_reason: The study cites Arditi et al. and borrows the general idea of directional ablation, but it never identifies, ablates or adds a harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction. Its only ablations erase Jacobian-lens directions of false entity tokens in a factual-falsehood task. The CEM protocol is a vocabulary-space logit difference between compliance and caution pivot tokens, averaged over layers 19–29. That is a lean toward refusal or caution words, not a harmfulness representation measured apart from a refusal mechanism. Most of its categories (sycophancy, copyright, hallucination, impartiality) are not harm judgments, and the CEM step has no causal test. The behavioural rows are refusal counts only and show nothing about internal encoding. The paper states that no instance-level joint statistic links margin to behaviour. So no result bears on V5 or any other version as defined; the CEM finding is a related construct and is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct but incomplete. The authors conclude that behavioural evaluation is uninformative on 63.7% of pairs. They find an internal Jacobian-lens margin separating risky from control prompts in two Holm-surviving categories, which they call correlational, with no causal step. Separately, Minerva swallows presupposed falsehoods on 18 of 25 facts versus 1–4 under other framings. Ablating the false-token lens direction restores the truth in 11 of 25 suppressed cases versus 0 for the controls. A linear probe decodes truth at 77% accuracy, yet ablating its direction corrects nothing. They read this as dissociating linear decodability from causal control.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Jacobian-lens vocabulary-space contrastive score over risky/safe prompts, not a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation refusal direction; it does not ablate or add a refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: For the contrastive protocol, the dead-band ε = 1.0 was calibrated on 18 sycophancy pairs that are also part of the 124-pair set; the authors note that verdict labels, but not scores or t statistics, are partly circular. Per-category sample sizes are small (n = 10, and n = 4 for harm awareness), and only two categories survive Holm–Bonferroni correction.

fits_no_version.finding: In Minerva-7B-Instruct, a Jacobian-lens logit difference between compliance and caution pivot tokens leans more toward caution on risky prompts than on matched safe controls. This holds in 2 of 12 categories after Holm correction (sycophancy s=−1.10, confidentiality s=−1.04). Meanwhile, 63.7% of pairs show identical behaviour. The link between margin and behaviour is only qualitative.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal vocabulary-space caution signals can differentiate risky from safe prompts even when refusal or compliance behaviour is identical.

record.problems: Single model and one lens; the contrastive internal measurement is correlational and has no causal ablation; small and underpowered category samples; the dead-band calibration overlaps with evaluated sycophancy pairs; behavioral and internal-margin results are not joined with an instance-level statistic. The authors also state that the lens was fitted on 100 sequences and that the J-space covers only a small fraction of activation variance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the reported V5 contrastive-margin and paired-behavior results. The factual falsehood framing, entity-direction ablation, probe, and lens-comparison findings in Sections 6–7 were left out because they test factual knowledge/verbalization rather than refusal or the refusal direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction is computed, ablated or added; there is no capability check.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
No multi-direction or cone analysis of refusal.
No harmfulness representation is measured separately from a refusal direction. The CEM pivot-token margin conflates caution and refusal words, and there is no causal test.
One Italian instruct checkpoint only; no transfer tests.
Training explanations are hypotheses only; the base checkpoint was not run.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 link is over-generous. The CEM measures caution versus compliance word logits, not a harm judgment separate from refusal. Its categories are mostly not about harmfulness, and the internal and behavioural measures are never joined per pair. The study's only directional ablations concern factual entity tokens, not refusal. Appendix D lists Holm thresholds rather than adjusted p-values, consistent with the main table.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means refusal direction is identified or ablated; no refusal-inducing addition or general-capability test.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No jailbreak suppression of the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No test of whether refusal is affine, conic, or distributed across multiple refusal directions.

The paper measures risk-sensitive internal margins and behavior but does not establish a causal separation between a harmfulness judgment and a refusal mechanism; the paper also notes that no joint statistic was computed for the separate factual-robustness protocol.
Only one Italian instruct checkpoint is evaluated; no cross-language or cross-checkpoint transfer test.
Training-related explanations are hypotheses based on public documentation; no training data, stage, or reward-model intervention was run.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Sycophancy signal and confidentiality-disclosure risk categories
reader_labels.reason: The Jacobian-lens margin is significantly more cautious on risky than safe prompts in both corrected categories (R1–R2); the paper also reports many behaviorally identical paired outcomes, though it does not compute an instance-level joint statistic.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Only two categories survive multiplicity correction; the authors call other category results unproven and note small, underpowered per-category samples. The internal margin is correlational and does not establish that it causes refusal (R3–R12).
